title: Conclusion-to-evidence dependency graph (foundational)
description: Every cached conclusion records the exact evidence items it was derived from, forming a dependency graph with conclusions pointing at their supporting evidence. The graph is maintained incrementally as conclusions are added, so invalidation never requires a full rebuild. This is the foundation everything else in the tool rests on. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Knowledge Update and Invalidation Tool practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

t: Evidence change detection via version stamps (foundational)
title: Evidence change detection via version stamps (foundational)
description: Each evidence item carries a version stamp that changes on every edit. The tool compares current stamps against the stamps recorded when each conclusion was derived; any mismatch means the underlying evidence moved. Version stamps are cheap to check and never require re-reading full record contents. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Knowledge Update and Invalidation Tool practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Transitive invalidation by graph walk (foundational)
description: When evidence changes, a breadth-first walk follows reverse dependencies: the changed evidence invalidates its direct conclusions, which invalidate conclusions built on them, and so on. The walk marks each affected conclusion stale in a single pass, even across long derivation chains. Conclusions with no path from the change are untouched, so invalidation is surgical, not blanket. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Knowledge Update and Invalidation Tool practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Revalidation queue with priority (foundational)
description: Invalidated conclusions enter a revalidation queue ordered by importance: user-facing answers first, background analytics last. Each entry carries the changed evidence so revalidation can be incremental rather than from scratch. The queue is bounded; overflow drops the lowest-priority items with a note, since stale low-value conclusions are cheaper to recompute on demand. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
import heapq
q = []
for concl, prio in [('cA', 1), ('cB', 5), ('cC', 3)]:
    heapq.heappush(q, (prio, concl))
print('revalidation order:', [heapq.heappop(q)[1] for _ in range(len(q))])
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Knowledge Update and Invalidation Tool practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Staleness report for operators (foundational)
description: Each invalidation cycle ends in a staleness report: what changed, which conclusions were invalidated, which were revalidated clean, and which remain stale. The report gives operators a single place to see the blast radius of any evidence edit. Persistent staleness beyond a threshold escalates to a human review. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Knowledge Update and Invalidation Tool practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
